notes.meaning: The people of Jerusalem crowned Ahaziah as their new king because he was the only surviving son of Jehoram. Bandits raiding alongside an Arab force had already killed all of his older brothers. Even though he inherited the throne legitimately, his reign soon brought spiritual trouble to the nation.

Ahaziah began to rule Judah in 841 BC, but his reign lasted only one year. His mother was Athaliah, the granddaughter of King Omri of northern Israel. Because of this family connection, the royal court in Jerusalem was heavily influenced by the false worship of the northern kingdom.

Ahaziah copied the sinful practices of King Ahab's household instead of following the Lord. His own mother, Athaliah, urged him to adopt false gods like Baal. When parents teach wickedness rather than righteousness, their children often follow them into ruin.

Ahaziah did evil in God's eyes, just as the northern royal family had done. After his father died, he surrounded himself with advisers from Ahab's corrupt household. Listening to wicked voices in place of God's truth quickly led to his destruction.

Following the bad advice of his counselors, Ahaziah joined King Joram of Israel in a military campaign against King Hazael of Aram. They fought over the border town of Ramoth-gilead, a key trade location. During the fierce fighting, the Aramean army wounded Joram.

King Joram left the battlefield and went to the town of Jezreel to heal from his injuries. Because Ahaziah was Joram's close ally and nephew, he traveled down to Jezreel to visit him. This personal visit placed Ahaziah directly in harm's way.

Ahaziah's trip to visit the wounded king ended in disaster through the providence of God. When Ahaziah reached Jezreel, he rode out with Joram to confront Jehu. God had already chosen and anointed Jehu to carry out judgment on Ahab's evil family line.

As Jehu carried out God's judgment against Ahab's relatives, he ran into Judah's officials and royal kinsmen who served Ahaziah. Jehu put them all to death on the spot. Joining hands with evil people often brings shared judgment upon those who follow them.

Jehu's men tracked down Ahaziah, who was hiding in Samaria, and killed him. They still gave him a respectful burial because his grandfather Jehoshaphat had sought the Lord with all his heart. With his death, the royal family was left without any strong heir who was ready to govern.

As soon as Queen Athaliah discovered that her son Ahaziah was dead, she moved to kill all the royal heirs of Judah. She wanted to destroy David's royal line and seize the crown for herself. Her ruthless greed nearly wiped out the family through which God had promised the future Savior.

Princess Jehoshabeath bravely rescued baby Joash, a son of Ahaziah, right as the other royal children were being murdered. She hid the infant and his nurse in a room where bedding was kept. Because she was married to the high priest Jehoiada, she had access to safe hiding spots and shielded Joash from Athaliah's deadly search.

Little Joash stayed secretly hidden with the priest's family in the temple living quarters for six years. During that whole time, Athaliah reigned over the land of Judah without knowing an heir had survived. God faithfully protected the young king in His own house until the time was right to reveal him.
